Zuhlsdorf, B., Buhler, F., Bantle, M. and Elmegaard, B. (2019). Analysis of technologies and potentials for heat pump-based process heat supply above 150 degC. Energy Conversion and Management: X, 2, 100011. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ecmx.2019.100011

Locators are printed article page numbers (page 1 = PDF page 1). The printed first author is Zuhlsdorf (not Bless or Arpagaus). A simulation study of two high-temperature heat pump concepts (multi-stage R-718 steam compression cascade; R-744 reversed Brayton) in two cases (alumina refining, 50 MW, 140-280 degC; spray dryer, 8.2 MW, air 64-210 degC). Loaded as heat-pump_industrial: for each concept x case the COP (Table 7, stored as % = COP x 100), TCI and specific TCI (Table 6, 2017 EUR via CEPCI), capacity, output temperature, 20-year life, 5% rate and derived capacity factor, plus the levelized heat cost for the alumina case; design limits of both concepts; and the comparator boilers of Table 5 (electric, gas, biogas, biomass: efficiency, specific capital cost, levelized heat cost). Subsystem TCIs, NPV, payback, IRR, cycle pressures and temperatures and price scenarios are in other-values. Not loaded: Figures 9-11 (levelized cost and NPV curves, charts), cost-function constants (Table 4), appendix state points. Overlap: arpagaus_2018_001 and iea-hpt_2023_001 hold product-level data; no row here duplicates them (iea-hpt cites this paper).
